lines.A: Any signed-in user except Read Only users, who are refused.
lines.C1: The user's existing password is removed from the account, when there are no password validation problems.
lines.C2: The new password is set on the account, when the removal succeeded and there are no password validation problems.
lines.S: The user clicks Save on the password form, which is enabled only once the form is valid and has been edited or touched.
lines.X1: Stops with a permission-denied message if the user changes their own password without the change-password permission or admin rights, or if the account is not found.
lines.X2: Stops with a permission-denied message if a non-admin tries to change someone else's password, or lacks change-password permission for their own, or the account is not found.
lines.X3: Stops with an error if a non-admin leaves the old password empty, or when an earlier permission check or missing account would already have stopped it.
lines.X4: Stops with a message that the account is managed by the single sign-on provider, when that provider is enabled and syncs user settings.
lines.X5: Stops with an invalid-password message when a user changing their own password gives an old password that is wrong.
lines.X6: Stops and shows the list of errors when the new password fails the password checks.
lines.X7: Stops with an error response when the user holds one of the roles the action is closed to.
lines.X8: Stops with a not-authenticated error when the signed-in user's identity cannot be read from the sign-in.

lines.C1: The new user record is saved to the database.
lines.C2: The new account is created in the sign-in system, when the email is present, valid and the admin is found.
lines.C3: Default home page dashboard sections are saved for the new user.
lines.C4: Default side navigation entries are saved for the new user.
lines.C5: The new user's preferences are saved again, when they include book reader highlight slots.
lines.C6: A default reading profile is saved for the new user.
lines.C7: Each chosen valid role is added to the new account, when account creation succeeded.
lines.C8: An invite email is sent in the background, when the email address is valid and email is set up on the server.
lines.S: An admin clicks the Invite button in the invite form.
lines.X1: Stops with a permission-denied message when the inviting admin cannot be found.
lines.X2: Stops with an invalid-request message when no email address is given.
lines.X3: Stops saying the user is already registered when the invited email already belongs to a confirmed account.
lines.X4: Stops and shows the errors when creating the account fails.
lines.X5: Stops and shows the errors when adding a role to the account fails.
lines.X6: Stops with a generic invite-failure message when no confirmation token could be produced.
lines.X7: Stops with a generic invite-failure message when something unexpected goes wrong.
lines.X8: Stops with a generic invite-failure message when the email checks report problems.

click-inviteusercomponent-invite.title: Invite a new user by email

lines.A: Users with access to the series who are not Read Only; Read Only users are refused.
lines.C1: The parent reading profile is updated with the new settings, when a profile exists.
lines.S: The user clicks the Save to button to update the parent reading profile.
lines.X1: Stops with not found when no series is identified and the user is not an admin.
lines.X2: Stops with not found when the user has no access to the series.
lines.X3: Stops with a not-authenticated error when the signed-in user's identity cannot be read.
lines.X4: Stops with an error response when the user holds a role the action is closed to.
lines.X5: Stops with a profile-does-not-exist error when no profile is found.

click-mangareadercomponent-updateparentp.title: Save reading settings to the parent profile

lines.A: Users who have access to the series.
lines.S: The user triggers a reload of the related series section on the series page.
lines.X1: Stops with not found when no series is identified and the user is not an admin.
lines.X2: Stops with not found when the user has no access to the series.
lines.X3: Stops with a not-authenticated error when the signed-in user's identity cannot be read.

lines.A: The system itself runs it on its daily schedule; no user starts it.
lines.S: A scheduled job runs the want-to-read cleanup once a day.
The user opens the All Annotations page in the browse area.
lines.X1: Users who are not logged in are sent to the login page.
lines.X2: Stops with an error when an unsupported kind of item is requested.

lines.S: The user opens the Browse Genres page.
lines.X1: Users who are not logged in are sent to the login page.

lines.A: Users who can access the reading list, including promoted lists.
lines.S: The user opens a reading list page.
lines.X1: Users who are not logged in are sent to the login page.
lines.X2: A missing or zero list id sends the user to the home page.
lines.X3: If the reading list is not found, the user is sent to the home page.
lines.X4: If loading the reading list fails, the user is sent to the home page.
lines.X5: Stops with a message that the reading list is restricted when it cannot be found for the user.
lines.X6: Stops with not found when no list is identified and the user is not an admin.
lines.X7: Stops with not found when the user has no access to the list.
lines.X8: Stops with a not-authenticated error when the signed-in user's identity cannot be read.
